fact: The second star of the Great Dog — and once the brightest ultraviolet beacon in our sky.
bio: Adhara (Epsilon Canis Majoris) is a hot blue-white pair about 430 light-years away, the second-brightest star in Canis Major after Sirius. A few million years ago it passed much closer to the Sun and was then the brightest star in Earth's entire sky.
cultural: The traditional name comes from an Arabic term for 'the maidens'. Though outshone today by its neighbour Sirius, Adhara remains a powerful source of ultraviolet light illuminating the surrounding interstellar gas.
